name: City Council Workshop
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council Budget Workshop

  June 22, 2009

A Budget Workshop of the City Council of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to
order by Mayor Ury at 5:03 p.m., on June 22, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo,
California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 19, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B, Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  Terence Boga, Assistant City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations -- The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are
  the City and City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

City Council Minutes  1  June 22, 2009
 At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

Mayor Ury announced that the Council provided direction to staff but there was nothing to report
from Closed Session.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

John Brault and Mike Krufra, representing Viejo Little League, M.V.: announced that Viejo
Little League serves over 400 families with children ranging in age from 4 to 14. They thanked
City staff for a fantastic job maintaining the seven baseball fields at Gilleran Park and requested
that the City continue to provide funding for baseball fields to the extent possible.

Jack Keady, M.V.: addressing his comments to Council Member Schlicht, he expressed concern
with her character assassinations of fellow Council Members. He asked Council Member
Schlicht to set an example for the youth in the City and to change her demeanor.

BUDGET WORKSHOP

1.  Review of Proposed 2009-2011 City Budget

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented an
  overview of the Proposed 2009-2001 Budget.

  The following expressed support for the low impact water aerobics program at Sierra
  Recreation Center and asked that it not be eliminated from the budget: Penny Young,
  M.V. and Nan MacAndrew, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in favor of continued funding for the Sierra
  Recreation Center water aerobics program: Judi Hasselkus, M.V.; Wilma McAllister
  Mille, M.V.; Christine Browning, M.V.; Jeanne Hatner, M.V.; Marilyn Kezmoh, M.V.;
  Ruth Rogers, M.V.; and Lorraine Kobett, M.V.

  Jack Keady, M.V.: stated that the City’s Recreation Centers benefit young and old, add to
  our property values and, in tough economic times, recreation has a great community
  bonding effect. Mr. Keady requested that the City keep the recreation and tennis centers
  as adequately funded as possible.

City Council Minutes  2  June 22, 2009
   Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle announced that there are no
  program cuts planned at the Sierra Recreation Center.

  The City Council Members asked questions and requested information on various items,
  including: an estimate to conclude the Montanoso traffic calming project; information on
  the replacement of the Aquatics Center (Nadadores) pool decking and a timeline for
  completion of that project; a summary of proposed Heritage Committee funding; an
  update on the City’s General Plan and carbon footprint; additional information on the
  costs being charged to the City for Sheriff positions; the cost to study the SR-73/SR-241
  Connector and direction for staff to explore the status of other agencies' interest in
  supporting the project; a report on whether or not the City can collect franchise fees on
  Cox cable or internet services; the cost to audit the Southern California Edison Franchise;
  consideration of paying down principal on the City’s debt, specifically the library bonds;
  the condition of City streets; direction to maintain the budget for arterial street sweeping
  once a week instead of modifying the schedule to a bi-weekly sweep; and whether there
  are ways to reduce the cost of the $700,000 SVUSD recreation program contract.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to include the
  Olympiad Road Olympic finish line project in the budget.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley and Ledesma
  NOES:  Schlicht, MacLean, and Ury
  ABSENT: None

  Council Member Schlicht expressed her concern that we are not really studying ways to
  reduce the budget. She recommended looking at the expenditures we make on behalf of
  Aliso Viejo for use of our animal shelter, the number of consultants we hire, reduction in
  library programs, reductions in the Kids Factory Program, and consideration of
  privatizing the library.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht to look for ways to reduce costs for the Kids
  Factory Program. Motion died for lack of a second.

2.  2009-11 Budget Workshop - Public Input

  By consensus, the City Council Members received and filed the public input messages as
  part of the budget review process.

City Council Minutes  3  June 22, 2009
 3.  Mission Viejo Dog Park

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Dave Gove, M.V.: expressed support for a dog park but asked the City to remove Oso
  Viejo Park from the list of possible sites.

  Bob Giritz, M.V.: stated that he is opposed to the idea of a dog park near La Tierra
  Elementary school at Sycamore Park.

  The following spoke in support of a dog park and expressed a willingness to explore
  options with the City: Susan Sellers, M.V.; Corissa Sellers, M.V.; Ben Sellers, M.V.; Ivy
  Melton, M.V.; and Joey Sellers, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in favor of a dog park: Nancy Hetzke, M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  refer this matter to the Community Services Commission to evaluate location, budget,
  size, and to see if we can't find an area where a compromise can be brokered. The City
  Council requested that the Commission endeavor to maintain a budget of approximately
  $250,000 and directed staff to return with a report outlining the Commission
  recommendations within 3-4 months.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

4.  Marguerite Aquatics and Tennis Centers Master Plan

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  Larry Ryan, RJM Design Group, Inc.: outlined the proposed Marguerite Aquatics and
  Tennis Centers Master Plan and the various options that have been considered.

  Council Member Schlicht suggested that the Council refer this to the Planning and
  Transportation Commission so residents' concerns can be addressed.

  The following spoke in opposition to several key elements of the master plan, but stated
  that they are not universally opposed: Larry Lesser, M.V.; Scott Haase, M.V.; Rolan

City Council Minutes  4  June 22, 2009
   Graham, M.V.; Bill Bonsall, M.V.; Suzanne McCord, MV.; Barbara Anderson, M.V.;
  and Tina Bach, M.V.

  The following presented a written comment in opposition to the project as proposed: John
  Croker, M.V.

  The following spoke in support of the project as proposed or with some modifications:
  Kime Goodrum, M.V.; Wil Garcia, M.V.; Wendy Bucknum, M.V.; Jan Kajvich; M.V.;
  Rudy Corrales, M.V.; Tom Teichmann, M.V.; Patti Bennett, M.V.; Tim Block, M.V.;
  Simon Hartigan, M.V.; Robert Guy, M.V.; Greg Silver, M.V.; and Brian Goodell, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in favor of the project: Tamara Chandler,
  M.V. Charles Chandler, M.V. Catherine M. Kerns, M.V.; Gloria Byrne, M.V.; Debra
  Griffith, M.V.; Tom Ross, M.V.; and Rochelle Lawrence, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  (1) approve the Community Services Commission’s recommendation to approve the
  Marguerite Aquatics and Tennis Centers Master Plan; (2) approve the Community
  Services Commission’s motion recommending approval of Phase 1 and Phase 2 as the
  base bid and Phase 3 and Phase 4 as bid alternatives for construction of the Marguerite
  Tennis Center Renovations Project (CIP 501); (3) issue a Purchase Order to RJM Design,
  Inc. for architectural services and preparation of contract bid documents in the amount of
  $348,000; (4) enter into a contract with Hodge and Associates for environmental services
  in the amount of $38,110; (5) enter into a contract with Friess Construction, Inc. for
  construction management services in the amount of $149,040; and (6) amend the master
  plan to review all the parking concerns, specifically preservation of tennis center parking
  spaces and minimizing asphalt in the parking area by utilizing more gravel and less
  formal spaces. Staff was directed to return with a report addressing parking issues as
  soon as possible.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

STAFF REPORTS

City Attorney’s Report

5.  Consideration of Resolution Regarding O’Neill Elementary School

City Council Minutes  5  June 22, 2009
   City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Robert Bennett, M.V: stated that he was representing O’Neill parents, Dean homeowners
  as well as citizens of the community. Mr. Bennett expressed support for the proposed
  resolution as a method for sending an important, meaningful, and respectful message to
  the School Board. He feels that the methodology surrounding the O’Neill school closures
  was not done in an appropriate fashion and his group is strongly motivated to preserve it
  as a residential school site. They are also willing to work with the Saddleback School
  District to establish a Charter School at this historic location.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to adopt Resolution
  09-26 Supporting the Parents and Residents Seeking to Preserve O’Neill Elementary
  School as an Elementary School and Support for Investigating Creation of a Charter
  School.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

ADJOURNMENT

  At the hour of 10:07 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City
  Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, July 6, 2009, at
  5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 6, 2009

City Council Minutes  6  June 22, 2009
